admin.title: Admin user manual
admin.intro: Use this guide when configuring Qlicker for your institution or helping instructors and students.
admin.summary: The admin dashboard saves after short pauses, so review sensitive values like SSO certificates, storage credentials, backup policy, newly issued 2-hour session defaults, and video settings carefully before leaving a tab.
quickStart: Confirm institution-wide defaults in Settings before a new term starts.
Configure backup, storage, SSO, and video in the admin UI before onboarding users when your deployment depends on shared services.
Use the Users and Courses tabs to verify that roles, enrollments, and active courses match reality.

sections.title: Start with the required formats and deployment assumptions
sections.subtitle: Most admin problems come from a small mismatch between expected field formats and the environment.
bullets: Run the server, client, and database with the deployment environment values you actually plan to support before testing admin workflows.

Allowed email domains are a comma-separated list; login/session expiry is a whole number of minutes for newly issued access and refresh sessions; locale, date format, and time format become global defaults.
SSO values are plain text fields for URLs, entity IDs, and attribute names. Certificates and keys should be pasted exactly as your identity provider supplies them.
Storage forms expect the provider-specific fields shown in the UI, and you should always confirm the setup by uploading an image afterward.
Use the Backup tab to confirm the scheduled backup time, the 7 daily / 4 weekly / 12 monthly retention defaults, and the latest run status before relying on the system for recovery.
In Profile, choose Light or Dark under Appearance. The setting saves automatically and follows your account across sessions and devices.
sections.note: When someone reports a user-facing issue, compare this guide with the professor or student guide so the support answer matches the current workflow.

screenshot.title: Admin dashboard overview
screenshot.description: The dashboard groups institution settings into focused tabs so you can audit one area at a time.

sections.title: Configure local, S3, or Azure storage correctly
sections.subtitle: Storage now lives in the database, but the cloud provider still has to be ready.
bullets: New deployments start on local storage by default, and the selected backend is saved in Qlicker's Settings document rather than in runtime environment variables.
Local storage is the simplest option, but the server environment must preserve uploaded files safely across restarts and deployments.
Amazon S3 mode needs bucket, region, access key ID, secret key, and optional endpoint plus path-style support for compatible services such as MinIO.
Azure Blob mode needs storage account, access key, and container name. The bucket or container must already exist and allow the app to read and write.
Set the maximum upload width to control image resizing before upload. The default is 1920px.
Set the avatar thumbnail size to control how large cropped profile thumbnails are generated. The default is 512px.
After saving storage changes, upload a sample image from the rich-text editor and the profile page, then confirm both the full image and avatar thumbnail render correctly.
sections.warning: Treat storage keys and private credentials as secrets. Rotate them if they are exposed.

screenshot.title: Storage configuration preview
screenshot.description: Switch providers in the Storage tab and fill only the fields that apply to the chosen backend.

sections.title: Set up SSO and institution-wide video before opening access broadly
sections.subtitle: These settings affect how people enter the platform and how instructors use real-time tools.
bullets: Enable SSO only after you have the identity provider entry point, logout URL, entity ID, attribute mappings, and the correct certificates or private keys.
Paste certificates and private keys exactly as issued. Private keys usually include BEGIN and END markers and should not be edited by hand.
Leave the advanced SAML settings on their defaults unless your IdP requires something different. The default route set presented to the IdP remains the legacy /SSO/SAML2 surface.
If another IdP expects the newer /api/v1/auth/sso callback/logout routes, switch the route mode only after retesting metadata, login, callback, and logout end to end.
Enable Jitsi only after the Jitsi domain and optional Etherpad domain are correct, then choose which courses can use video.
Retest login, logout, and a video-enabled course after every change so instructors are not surprised during class time.
sections.warning: Incorrect SSO values can block sign-in for every user, so make changes during a maintenance window whenever possible.

sections.title: Manage users, courses, and role-based support
sections.subtitle: Once global settings are correct, the Users and Courses tabs become your daily support tools.
bullets: Search users by name or email, change roles, verify email addresses, create accounts, reset local passwords, and open per-user properties when local email login or professor promotion rules must change.
Disable a user when you need to block sign-in without erasing the account history, then restore the same account later if access should return.
When institution-wide SSO is enabled, non-admin users need the per-account allow-email-login exception before local email sign-in and password-reset email become available.
Review courses and user details to confirm the correct student, TA, and instructor memberships, term labels, activity state, and enrollment readiness before troubleshooting a professor workflow.
Student-only users who teach a course appear as TAs in the admin UI, but that is presentation-only wording rather than a new stored role.
Admins can open the professor and student manuals directly from the manual switcher on these pages, which is helpful when reproducing a reported issue from another role's point of view.

Open Users → Manage notifications, enter Title and Message at the top, choose all users, students, or profs under Send to, set the dates, then Post notification and Confirm. The avatar menu's Notifications is a read-only inbox, not the composer; notices are in-app, not email.
sections.warning: Role changes and SSO login approvals take effect immediately, so confirm the request before saving.

sections.title: Monitor host load and busy teaching periods
sections.subtitle: Open Usage Statistics and compare CPU, memory, network, and recent-user history.
bullets: Select 6 hours, 24 hours, or 7 days. Use Refresh to fetch new samples; the page does not continuously poll. Hover or tap a history chart to inspect the nearest time bucket and each curve's value. Focus the chart and use Left/Right or Home/End; Escape dismisses the readout. Missing values are marked No reading, never interpolated.
CPU and memory cover the entire Linux host. Network shows received/sent bytes per second on the selected host interfaces. Other applications on the host contribute to these values.

Recently active means a unique user made an authenticated API request in the preceding 15 minutes by default. It does not count every signed-in browser. Idle users age out and role counts can overlap. The memory card shows used, total, and available RAM. Automatic network selection prefers non-tunnel default-route interfaces to avoid counting both VPN and uplink traffic. Check the displayed interface names; network rates use KiB/s or MiB/s, not bits per second.
History starts when the system-monitor service is installed and expires after seven days. Charts average resource measurements in 1-, 5-, or 30-minute buckets and show the maximum sampled user count.
Compare Peak periods with the charts. Check the latest sample time and Monitor events for stale data, errors, or recovery. Full Docker service logs remain available to deployment operators.
sections.note: Example data shown in a real browser capture; use your own history to investigate incidents.

professor.title: Professor user manual
professor.intro: Use this guide to create courses, organize questions, run sessions or quizzes, and interpret student results.
professor.summary: Good course topics and consistent semester names make almost every later workflow easier: search, copying, import/export, and grading all benefit from a tidy course structure.
quickStart: Create the course with a consistent semester name such as Fall 2026 or Winter 2027.
Add course topics first, then set up groups if you plan to use them for in-class organization or reporting.
Build sessions from the course page, decide which ones are interactive or quiz-based, and review results after students have participated.

sections.title: Create a course and add topics before you scale up
sections.subtitle: A clean course setup saves time when you copy or search later.
bullets: The course creation dialog combines a semester season and year into one label, which you can edit later if you need a custom or legacy format. Search sessions starts expanded and can be collapsed. Enabling chat or AI keeps Course Settings selected; Back to course restores the originating tab. Show Stats follows new attempts in the presentation window without reloading.
Use course settings to manage the title, enrollment rules, quiz time display, active state, and whether students may access practice questions, the course question library, and practice sessions.
Add course topics early so your own questions stay organized and students can search the library material you make visible to them when practice-question access is enabled.

Each course has an enrollment or join code that students enter from their dashboard to join that specific course. Share the current code with your class and update it in course settings if you need to stop an old code from being reused.

Open the course's Students or Instructors tab → Manage notifications. Enter Title and Message at the top; choose everyone in this course to include students and instructors, or target either group. Set the dates, then Post notification and Confirm. The avatar menu's Notifications is a read-only inbox; no email is sent.
sections.note: If you teach similar courses each term, use the same naming convention so copied material remains easy to identify.

screenshot.title: Professor course workspace preview
screenshot.description: Course pages gather sessions, settings, question-library tools, and grades into one workspace.

sections.title: Set up groups before you need them in class
sections.subtitle: Groups work best when categories and membership are prepared before a live session begins.
bullets: Use the Groups tab on the course page to create a category, choose how many groups it should contain, and rename groups if you want clearer labels than the defaults.
Each student can belong to only one group inside a category, but the same course can have multiple categories for different activities or labs.
Add or remove students directly in the group management view, or import a CSV when you already have a roster prepared in spreadsheet form.
Download the CSV export when you want a record of the current group makeup or when you want a starting point for editing and re-uploading membership.
If you use groups for participation analysis or group-specific activities, verify the membership before launching the relevant session.
sections.note: Groups are course-specific, so copied sessions do not replace the need to review group categories in the destination course.

sections.title: Build sessions with questions, slides, and visibility in mind
sections.subtitle: Sessions are ordered learning flows, not just containers.
bullets: Use the session editor to set the session name, description, visibility, reviewability, passcode requirement, quiz window, extensions, and multi-select scoring method. Create tags in Course Settings, then select the tags that describe this session and its questions.
Add new questions, pick from the question library, import session JSON, or insert slides anywhere in the sequence.
Slides are content-only pages, so they are ideal for instructions, worked examples, or discussion prompts between graded questions.
Question visibility matters: keep private content private, share course-public material intentionally, and use Qlicker-wide visibility only when broad reuse is really desired.
Use Expand all previews or Collapse all previews above the question list, or toggle an individual question preview.

Use Grades visible beside Reviewable in the session list, editor, or review page to release scores without opening session review. Reviewable turns grade visibility on or off with it. While Reviewable is off, you can explicitly release grades. Release is available after the session and any extensions end.
sections.warning: Once a question has response data, some edits are intentionally restricted to protect the meaning of past results.

screenshot.title: Session editor preview
screenshot.description: The session editor keeps ordering, settings, and import/export actions together so you can build a complete activity in one place.

sections.title: Use the rich-text editor for math, images, and clear prompts
sections.subtitle: Questions, slides, solutions, and some feedback fields all support rich content.
bullets: Use formatting tools like bold, lists, colors, links, and code only when they make the prompt easier to read, not busier.
Simple LaTeX examples include $a^2+b^2=c^2$, $\frac{1}{2}$, and $$\int_0^1 x^2\,dx=\frac{1}{3}$$.
Upload images directly in the editor, resize them for readability, and preview the rendered result before publishing.
Keep your wording concise so students can focus on the concept rather than on deciphering the prompt.

sections.title: Use the library, import/export, and copy tools to prepare efficiently
sections.subtitle: Once the course structure is in place, reuse becomes one of the fastest ways to prepare.
bullets: Use the question library to search by course, type, tags, sessions, and approval state; export or import JSON bundles when sharing content.
Copy sessions within a course or across your courses after checking that the destination course topics still make sense for the imported material.
Review imported or copied content before class so visibility, passcodes, quiz dates, and tags match the destination course.

sections.title: Run interactive sessions and quizzes intentionally
sections.subtitle: Different session types are best for different teaching moments.
bullets: Interactive sessions are for live teaching: you control navigation, response windows, statistics, answer reveals, attempts, and the presentation window. Individual extensions work after a quiz is Ended. Active or upcoming extensions block review; granting one disables existing review and hides published grades. After extensions finish, recalculate grades before publishing again. Extensions do not unlock submitted quizzes.

For short-answer questions, the professor control view always keeps the full response list visible; a separate toggle controls whether students and the presentation window see that shared list. The presentation window follows numbered question buttons as well as Previous/Next, including visibility, statistics, correct answers, and new attempts. Student names remain anonymous in presentation chat and responses; reconnecting restores the current classroom state.

Quizzes are scheduled windows where students answer on their own timeline. Use start and end times plus extensions for accommodation workflows. The course and editor status menus control the same setting. Choosing Live opens the quiz regardless of dates and keeps the editor open, with a link to live results. Choose date-controlled status to follow the schedule, or Ended to close general access while preserving individual extensions.
Practice quizzes feel more like guided rehearsal and are well suited for self-study or optional reinforcement.
If a session depends on passcodes, groups, or visible statistics, confirm those settings before students begin joining.

Session lists keep search, filters, and pagination inside Search sessions. While an interactive session is live, opening its card joins the live controls directly; live quiz cards still open the editor.

Responses and attendance are stored without student identities. This session will not be graded. Anonymity cannot be changed after students have joined or responded. Anonymous live statistics and unlinked answer lists update after at least four new people respond to the question and attempt. Names and answer times are hidden. After the activity ends, answers are released separately for each question and attempt with at least four respondents, linked across eligible questions. Smaller groups show their actual response count with an answers-hidden notice; overall percentages remain hidden while any answers are withheld. Unique answers may still identify someone. An information banner in the live Controls explains the four-person minimum while statistics are hidden, then shows the released response count and batching rule.

The session editor shows sharing controls only when the course allows activity sharing. Use the session switch to turn sharing on or off; the active code remains visible after a refresh and can be regenerated. First enable activity-code sharing in Course settings; it is off by default. Turning it off revokes existing codes and outside access. Remove individual quiz extensions before sharing; they remain unavailable after sharing. To invite signed-in people outside the course, create a quiz or live session in the course and generate an S- activity code in its editor. Copy it when shown; regenerating stops new use of the old code, and disabling revokes outside access. Turning sharing back on reuses the same code; only Regenerate code replaces it. In a named activity, enrolled students can receive grades; guests have tracked responses but no grade items. Turn on anonymity for a survey with no grade items for anyone. Choose named or anonymous responses before anyone redeems the code. After the activity ends, answers are released separately for each question and attempt with at least four respondents, linked across eligible questions. Smaller groups show their actual response count with an answers-hidden notice; overall percentages remain hidden while any answers are withheld. Unique answers may still reveal someone. The rotating live join code still applies when enabled. Activity codes do not work while the activity is in Draft, even for previous participants. The same code becomes usable when the instructor publishes the activity. Activity codes use S- followed by seven letters or digits. The active code also appears in the instructor’s live session controls.

If an instructor changes a live session to Upcoming, participants see a waiting screen until it returns to Live. Draft sends enrolled students back to the course and guests back to their dashboard. Saved answers are preserved.

For an Upcoming interactive session, students can select Open waiting page; guests can enter its S- activity code. Waiting does not record attendance. The instructor can still edit the session and require a live join code. When the session goes Live, participants wait for a question or enter the join code once the instructor opens the join period.

sections.title: Use join codes for attendance and admission
sections.subtitle: Control entry to a live interactive session, then handle late arrivals individually.
bullets: The course enrollment code joins the course; the six-digit session join code admits an already-enrolled student to one live session. For attendance-controlled entry, enable Require Passcode before students join.

When an interactive session becomes Live, Qlicker selects the first question or slide if none is active. An existing active item is preserved. A newly selected first item starts hidden until you reveal it, just as with Launch. Launch does not open admission automatically. In the live Controls, enable Join Period and use Open presentation window to show the current code in class. Students open the live session and enter that code.

Set Refresh (sec) between 5 and 120; keep the professor's live controls open for automatic rotation. Refresh join code replaces the code immediately. Students not yet admitted must enter the current code.
After check-in, turn off Join Period but leave Require Passcode enabled. Without the passcode requirement, enrolled students can join a running session without a code.

For a late arrival, open Students, expand Waiting to join, filter by name or email, and select Admit beside the verified student. They must be enrolled. Manual admission works while the session is running even with Join Period closed.
Waiting to join lists enrolled students who have not joined, not necessarily people online or requesting admission.

Admission persists for that session, whether by code or by an instructor. Students can leave, refresh, lose connection, and rejoin the running session with the same account without another code—even after rotation or closing Join Period. Enabling passcodes later does not remove earlier admissions; a different session requires its own admission.
sections.warning: Use an in-class code and a short check-in window to support attendance enforcement. A shared code or joined count does not prove physical presence or continued attendance; also review participation and apply your institution's policy.

sections.title: Review results, grade consistently, and communicate feedback
sections.subtitle: After students participate, Qlicker gives you several ways to inspect outcomes and respond.
bullets: Session review lets you inspect results, response data, grading state, and student summaries. Live interactive sessions can be reviewed while they are still running, but grading stays locked until the session ends. Response Data shows points only when a question has an actual grade mark; a recorded zero is still shown. Anonymous respondents and ungraded guests have no point suffix. Responses by question uses the same question navigator and full preview as grading, including options, correct answers, and an optional solution, without grade-editing controls.
Grades show participation, automatic marks, and manual-grading needs. Recalculate grades when scoring rules change or when you want automatic results rebuilt.

Grading requires an Ended session, expired or removed extensions, and grade items. Ending creates grade items; scheduled quizzes close after the last time window when accessed. Use Create grade items if they are missing. Nonblank short answers need grading until a score is saved, including zero. Only missing or blank answers receive zero automatically. Publishing recalculates automatic grades and preserves manual overrides.
The results tab now shows each student's actual session grade before participation, and clicking a student's avatar in the Students tab opens the larger profile photo.
Grade detail dialogs now label question rows with both number and type, such as Q1(MC) or Q2(SA), and visually highlight rows that still need grading while ignoring stale zero-point grading flags.
Students receive a notification when you publish new feedback, so use short, actionable comments that tell them what to revisit.
If group structures mattered during the activity, compare the review and grading data with the course groups so you can spot uneven participation patterns.

Enrollment creates missing grades for completed course activities, including saved guest responses. Missed work receives zero without needing grading; written answers may need grading. Existing grades and feedback are preserved. Anonymous activities remain ungraded.

Grade-table averages use actual grade items in the displayed sessions. Missing items are excluded; recorded zeros count. Use Select sessions with grade items, or include sessions labelled No grade items manually.
Only submitted quizzes are shown until this quiz ends. After it ends, saved answers are included even if the student did not submit.

In Response Data, Export CSV opens an options dialog. Select Include response timestamps to add a time column for each question and attempt. Times use ISO 8601 with the browser timezone and the offset at the response date, including daylight saving time. They indicate the last answer save, falling back to creation time, not final quiz submission. Missing legacy timestamps remain blank. Anonymous activities never export response times. The export keeps the table’s current search and sort order. The Joined Session CSV column always uses the same format. The suffix -04:00 means four hours behind UTC; the offset accounts for daylight saving time at the recorded date. Missing join times are blank.

In Results, the session response timeline is collapsed on page load and combines all questions and attempts. Each question attempt has its own expandable graph, using only that attempt’s response timestamps to set the range. Adjust Detail to change the interval size; hover, tap, or use the arrow keys to inspect counts. Charts span the recorded response times, including gaps and responses outside scheduled quiz dates. Dotted lines mark scheduled quiz dates within the plot; dates outside it are listed below. Quiz charts count each answer at its last saved time, not every edit or final quiz submission. Missing timestamps are counted but excluded, and anonymous activities do not show timelines.
sections.success: Professors can open the student manual from the switcher above to preview the learner workflow before class.

sections.title: Use course chat and session chat deliberately
sections.subtitle: Course chat supports ongoing discussion; session chat supports the activity happening right now.
bullets: Enable Course Chat and choose its retention period in Course Settings. The Course Chat tab then appears for both instructors and students.

Course chat is organized into titled, tagged topics with comments and upvotes. Instructors can filter by topic or author, sort discussions, and archive threads; students see anonymous role labels while instructors retain the identity needed for moderation.
Enable Session Chat from the live-session controls. You can separately disable rich-text posts and comments while keeping quick posts tied to the current question available.

Use session-chat upvotes to find common questions, dismiss a resolved thread without deleting it, and review the conversation after the session. Unseen-count badges help you notice activity while presenting.
Set expectations before class: use course chat for durable questions and resources, session chat for immediate confusion, and the answer controls for graded responses.

Guests who have joined a shared live activity can use its enabled session chat, including quick posts, comments, and votes. This does not grant access to course chat. In anonymous activities, other participants and instructors cannot see guest or student identities in chat. Avoid identifying yourself in message text.
Session chat shows the most recently active discussion first. A new post, comment, or upvote moves the discussion to the top. Unread badges clear when you open Chat.
sections.note: Chat visibility and author identity differ by role. Preview the student manual before introducing chat to the class.

sections.title: Use AI for course preparation, analysis, grading, and student support
sections.subtitle: Qlicker separates AI configuration, conversational tools, response summaries, and grading so you can control each use.
bullets: An administrator must authorize AI for the course before you can enable AI Helper in Course Settings. AI Settings then controls approved models, the instructor default, tool-round limits, and any course-specific backend the administrator permits.

Use AI Chat to inspect course sessions, rosters, questions, responses, grade tables, and course-chat discussions, or to create sessions and questions. New AI-generated questions are tagged Generated by AI and should be reviewed before use.

Edits to existing sessions or questions and AI-written course-chat posts are drafts. Read the exact proposed change and send its displayed approval phrase in a later message before Qlicker applies it; the assistant has no deletion tools.

In Session Review, generate an AI response summary for an individual question by choosing a model and a saved summary instruction. You can monitor, halt, regenerate, and view the result without changing grades.

In the Grading tab, use AI Grading Assistant only after saving separate grading and student-feedback instructions for each selected question. Review its progress, report, log, points, and feedback before making results visible.
Manage reusable grading, feedback, and summary instructions in AI Settings and copy them from another course when appropriate.

Student AI Chat is a separate opt-in. Choose student-approved models, a default, guidance, and a smaller tool-round limit; students can access only visible/reviewable course data and their own grades.
Save edited summary instructions before generating. The selected guidance controls the language, focus, and output format of each summarization stage.
sections.warning: AI output can be incomplete or wrong. Verify generated content, summaries, grades, feedback, dates, and proposed actions before relying on them.

sections.title: Use the profile page for language, password, and avatar changes
sections.subtitle: Account settings follow the same institution-wide auth rules as student accounts.
bullets: Uploading a profile picture opens a crop-and-rotate dialog so you can choose the square avatar thumbnail before saving.
When institution-wide SSO is enabled, your name and password fields remain locked unless an administrator has granted the allow-email-login exception for your account.
Password-reset email follows the same rule, so use the SSO route or contact an administrator if the profile page says local email login is disabled.
In Profile, choose Light or Dark under Appearance. The setting saves automatically and follows your account across sessions and devices.

student.title: Student user manual
student.intro: Use this guide to enroll in courses, join live activities, complete quizzes, review feedback, and build practice sessions.
student.summary: Your course page is the best starting point because it separates live activities, quizzes, practice sessions, review links, and library content into clear tabs.
quickStart: Enroll with the course code from your instructor.
Open the course page and check which tab contains the activity you need right now.
Use review pages and practice sessions to turn feedback into another round of learning.

sections.title: Enroll in a course and learn the course tabs
sections.subtitle: Most student work begins from the course dashboard.
bullets: Enter the enrollment code exactly as your instructor provides it. If the course is inactive, enrollment is rejected and you will need to try again after the course is activated. Search sessions starts expanded and can be collapsed.

The course page separates lectures or live sessions, quizzes, practice sessions, grades, and question-library material so you can find the right workflow quickly. In courses where practice-question access is disabled, the practice and library tabs stay hidden. Choose Reviewable in the status filter to show only ended sessions that your instructor has made available for review. Draft is not offered in the student filter.
Session lists keep search, filters, and pagination inside a collapsible Search sessions area so you can expand controls only when you need them.
If your institution requires verified email or SSO, finish that setup first before assuming the enrollment code is wrong.
You usually only need the join code once per course. After it works, the course stays on your dashboard until you are removed or the course is archived for your account.
Watch the badge on your avatar in the app bar for active notifications, then open Notifications from the account menu to read or dismiss them.

Choose Join activity on the dashboard and enter an S- activity code to open a quiz or live session without enrolling in its course. A live session may also require its rotating join code. If you are not enrolled in the course, your responses are tracked but you receive no grade. Enrolled students can receive grades in named activities; anonymous activities have no grades. Anonymous live statistics and unlinked answer lists update after at least four new people respond to the question and attempt. Names and answer times are hidden. After the activity ends, answers are released separately for each question and attempt with at least four respondents, linked across eligible questions. Smaller groups show their actual response count with an answers-hidden notice; overall percentages remain hidden while any answers are withheld. Unique answers may still identify someone. Activity codes do not work while the activity is in Draft, even for previous participants. The same code becomes usable when the instructor publishes the activity.

Enrollment creates missing grades for completed course activities, including saved guest responses. Missed work receives zero without needing grading; written answers may need grading. Existing grades and feedback are preserved. Anonymous activities remain ungraded.

sections.title: Join live sessions and understand how quizzes differ
sections.subtitle: Interactive sessions, quizzes, and practice sessions may look similar, but they behave differently.
bullets: Interactive sessions usually happen live. You may need a passcode, and your instructor decides when responses open, close, or show statistics. An individual extension lets you open, save and submit an ended quiz during your assigned window. Your course card shows your own deadline. It does not unlock a submitted quiz; review waits until all extensions end.
Quizzes have a defined time window and normally expect you to answer the whole set before final submission. Your work saves while you move between questions.
Practice sessions are for self-study and can feel more flexible because they are designed to help you rehearse instead of keeping pace with a live class.
Slides can appear between questions. They are content pages, so read them carefully before moving on.
If your instructor reveals statistics for a word cloud or histogram, the view should update automatically without a refresh.
For short-answer questions, the shared response list can be shown or hidden separately from the word cloud, so you may see one without the other.
Scrolling over a numerical answer leaves its value unchanged and moves focus out of the input so the page can scroll. Click or tab back into the input to continue editing.

An Anonymous label means your instructor sees your answers without your name. You still sign in and can answer each question only once, you can review your own answers later, and the session is not graded.

If an instructor changes a live session to Upcoming, participants see a waiting screen until it returns to Live. Draft sends enrolled students back to the course and guests back to their dashboard. Saved answers are preserved.

For an Upcoming interactive session, students can select Open waiting page; guests can enter its S- activity code. Waiting does not record attendance. The instructor can still edit the session and require a live join code. When the session goes Live, participants wait for a question or enter the join code once the instructor opens the join period.

sections.title: Use the response editor for text, math, and images when the question allows it
sections.subtitle: Some questions accept richer responses than plain text only.
bullets: Use the editor toolbar only when it makes your answer clearer, for example a short list, emphasis, or a clean link.
Simple math examples include $\frac{1}{2}$, $x^2+1$, or \(\sum_{i=1}^{n} i\). Use display math for expressions that deserve their own line.
If image uploads are available, attach clear photos or diagrams and avoid unrelated background details.
Preview what you typed when equations or symbols matter, because a small formatting mistake can change the meaning of your answer.

sections.title: Review sessions one question at a time and use feedback
sections.subtitle: Review mode is one of the best study tools in the app.
bullets: Open reviewable sessions from the course page after your instructor ends the activity and turns on review. Click a grade in the Grades table to open the session review.
Move one question at a time to compare your answer, the released answer, the explanation, and any instructor feedback without rushing past details.
Watch for feedback notifications because they tell you when new comments or grading updates are available.

Average grade and participation use all your visible grade items, including sessions that are not reviewable. Missing items are excluded; recorded zeros count. A grade opens session review only when Reviewable is on.
If no grades have been released, your averages show Not applicable even if your instructor has already graded your work.
sections.success: Students often improve fastest when they read the feedback and then immediately try a similar question again.

screenshot.title: Review and practice preview
screenshot.description: Review pages explain your results and help you decide what to practice next.

sections.title: Create your own practice sessions
sections.subtitle: Build a named study set from library questions or questions you write yourself.
bullets: Your instructor must enable access to practice questions. If the Question Library and Practice Sessions tabs are missing, ask your instructor; your own private library questions can also be used.
Open the course, choose Practice Sessions, then New practice session. Enter a required name, such as “Cell biology — revision for Quiz 2”, and optionally select Session tags.

Choose Add question → Copy from Question Library. Search or filter, select questions, and choose Add selected questions to practice session. For a mixed set, filter first, enter Random count, and choose Randomly add … questions from the list.
Use Add question above, below, or between questions to insert more. Remove excludes a question from the set without deleting the original library question.

To write your own question, choose Add question → Create New, select a type, and complete the prompt, answer options or expected answer, and solution. Wait for the save confirmation before closing the question editor. Use Edit to revise questions you own.

Choose Save and start practice to save the session and open its review. Try each question yourself before selecting Show Solution. This personal self-study workflow is separate from submitting an instructor's graded quiz.

Return to Practice Sessions to reopen your set, use Edit to rename it or change its questions, or Delete and confirm to remove it. If saving fails, check the error and required name before leaving the editor.
sections.note: Questions save separately from the session: cancelling the session editor does not undo question edits already saved. Start with a small topic-focused set, then create a mixed set using random selection.

sections.title: Use course chat and session chat for different kinds of questions
sections.subtitle: Course chat continues across the term; session chat follows a live activity.
bullets: The Course Chat tab appears only when your instructor enables it. Create a titled topic, add course-topic tags, comment on a thread, or upvote a useful question so it is easier to find.
Classmates appear anonymously in chat, while instructors retain the identity needed for moderation. You can edit or delete your own posts according to the available controls.

During a live activity, open the Chat panel for question-specific discussion. Quick posts remain available when the instructor disables rich-text posts; comments and upvotes depend on the current session settings.
A dismissed or archived discussion is not necessarily deleted. It is hidden from your student review afterward, but the teaching team can retain it for review and moderation.
Chat messages do not submit an answer. Return to the Question panel and use the response button whenever the activity is graded or participation is tracked.

Guests who have joined a shared live activity can use its enabled session chat, including quick posts, comments, and votes. This does not grant access to course chat. In anonymous activities, other participants and instructors cannot see guest or student identities in chat. Avoid identifying yourself in message text.
Session chat shows the most recently active discussion first. A new post, comment, or upvote moves the discussion to the top. Unread badges clear when you open Chat.

sections.title: Use student AI Chat safely and effectively
sections.subtitle: Student AI Chat appears only when the administrator and your instructor have enabled an approved model for the course.
bullets: Start a separate conversation for each study goal and choose only from the models your instructor approved. The instructor may also provide course-specific guidance for how the assistant should help.

The assistant can summarize the visible session schedule, inspect questions and solutions from reviewable sessions, and explain your own released grade and feedback. It cannot reveal draft sessions, hidden solutions, or another student's work.
Ask for explanations, comparisons, practice strategies, or help interpreting feedback. Include the session or topic name so the assistant can choose the right course information.
Generated images, audio, or files may expire, so download anything you are permitted to keep or ask the assistant to generate it again later.
Treat every answer as study support, not as the official course policy or answer key. Check important claims against the course material and ask your instructor when they disagree.
sections.warning: Do not paste passwords, private personal information, assessment answers you are not allowed to share, or other sensitive material into AI Chat.

sections.title: Update your profile, language, and avatar carefully
sections.subtitle: Profile settings depend on whether your institution uses SSO for the account.
bullets: Uploading a profile picture opens a crop-and-rotate dialog so you can position the avatar circle before saving.
If institution-wide SSO is enabled and your account has not been granted email-login access, your name and password fields stay locked on purpose.
In that same SSO-managed case, password-reset email is unavailable until an administrator grants the allow-email-login exception for your account.
In Profile, choose Light or Dark under Appearance. The setting saves automatically and follows your account across sessions and devices.
